name: Meropenem
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Complicated skin and skin structure infections
usual_adult_dose.dose: 500 mg IV every 8 hours (1 g every 8 hours if Pseudomonas aeruginosa)

key_interactions.effect: Valproate levels can fall below the therapeutic range; breakthrough seizures.
key_interactions.action: Generally not recommended; prefer a non-carbapenem; if needed, consider supplemental anticonvulsant.

key_interactions.effect: Competes for tubular secretion; higher meropenem levels.

common: Headache, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, anemia, vomiting, rash (≥2%)

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to product components or other drugs in the same class
Conditions where sodium or chloride would be harmful (premixed product)
monitoring: Seizure activity, especially with CNS disorders or kidney impairment

pk.peak: End of 30-minute infusion: about 23 mcg/mL (500 mg) and 49 mcg/mL (1 g)
pk.half_life_eskd: About 6.8 hours in ESKD (vs 0.9 hours healthy; Christensson 1992); 7.0 hours off dialysis, 2.9 hours during hemodialysis (Chimata 1993)
pk.metabolism: One microbiologically inactive metabolite (about 28% of dose)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 70% (50% to 75%) unchanged in urine within 12 hours
pk.dialyzability: Yes: readily dialyzable and effectively removed by hemodialysis (label); dialysis clearance about 79 mL/min/1.73 m2 (Christensson 1992).

sources.citation: B. Braun Medical Inc.. (2025). Meropenem and Sodium Chloride (meropenem and sodium chloride) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA202106, set ID 3b952a55-6ef7-45c8-be21-16eefe37ec2e, version effective August 5, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

Christensson, B. A., Nilsson-Ehle, I., Hutchison, M., Haworth, S. J., Oqvist, B., & Norrby, S. R. (1992). Pharmacokinetics of meropenem in subjects with various degrees of renal impairment. Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy, 36(7), 1532–1537.

Chimata, M., Nagase, M., Suzuki, Y., Shimomura, M., & Kakuta, S. (1993). Pharmacokinetics of meropenem in patients with various degrees of renal function, including patients with end-stage renal disease. Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy, 37(2), 229–233.

draft_notes: ESKD half-life is from two small 1990s PK studies (n=4 to 5 ESKD patients each), PubMed-verified; label has none.
Selected US label is the B. Braun premixed bag (NDA202106); the PH market is vials. Meningitis is a pediatric indication; consider dropping it from an adult-dose row.
Platelet monitoring in kidney impairment is our inference from label 5.9 (thrombocytopenia seen in renal impairment, no bleeding); the label sets no schedule.
